elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: The clause states: “The Company owns all deliverables ... created for the Company under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: The clause states: “The Company owns all ... work product created for the Company under this Agreement.”

elements.element: Vendor assigns all deliverables created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI “hereby assigns all such deliverables ... to the Company,” providing a present assignment.

elements.element: Vendor assigns all work product created for Customer to Customer.
elements.evidence: HDI “hereby assigns all such ... work product to the Company,” providing a present assignment.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states: “HDI retains its pre-existing intellectual property.”

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to all Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: HDI grants the Company a licence “to any HDI intellectual property embedded in such deliverables.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “perpetual.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “irrevocable.”

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The embedded-IP licence is expressly described as “royalty-free.”

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Company retains all rights in “all customer, order, user and other data belonging to, supplied by or processed for the Company.”

elements.element: No intellectual property is jointly owned by Customer and Vendor.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states: “No intellectual property shall be jointly owned by the Parties.”

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause preserves only HDI’s pre-existing intellectual property. It does not expressly preserve HDI ownership of generic tools generally, including generic tools developed during performance.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not mention or expressly preserve HDI ownership of generic know-how.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: The Company receives ownership of the deliverables, not an express licence to them. The only express licence covers HDI intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Perpetual duration applies only to the licence for embedded HDI intellectual property, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Irrevocability applies only to the licence for embedded HDI intellectual property, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide territorial scope is stated for any licence.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Royalty-free status applies only to the licence for embedded HDI intellectual property, not to a licence covering the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Although ownership generally provides broader control, the clause does not grant the specified express business-use licence to the deliverables.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no express licence right to modify the deliverables for the Company’s business.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no express licence right to sublicense the deliverables for the Company’s business.

result.reason: The redline fully implements the preferred ownership position through express ownership, present assignment, preservation of HDI’s pre-existing IP, the required embedded-IP licence, Customer Data rights, and a prohibition on joint ownership. The fallback is not independently satisfied because generic tools and know-how are not expressly reserved and no worldwide business-use, modification, and sublicensing licence to the deliverables is granted. The changes preserve the shown commercial terms and introduce no evident contradiction. They are not strictly minimal because the additional restriction limiting HDI’s use of Company data solely to providing the Services was not necessary to satisfy either stated position.
